full_judgment: 4. The Rule was duly served upon the two respondents. Moreover, the respondent No. 1, the financial institution, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the material allegations of the writ petition contending, inter alia, that since in the present Rule the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat has been challenged the same is not maintainable on the ground that in the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank and others, reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, it has been held by the Appellate Division that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree. Secondly, since no Power of Attorney was given by the mortgagor in favour of the mortgagee institution to sell the mortgaged property, hence, section 12 of the Ain is not applicable in the present case. He also referred to the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191 wherein it has been held "the suit against the petitioner being barred by limitation and in excess of the Court's jurisdiction are matters to be agitated in appeal and not under the writ jurisdiction". Hence, the Rule should be discharged.
